learning_outcomes.text: Recognize the fundamental principles of ethics and professional deontology in the field of engineering and technology.
Apply ethical decision-making models - such as consequentialism, virtue ethics and deontology - to solve professional dilemmas in engineering and technology.
Identify and critically analyze ethical dilemmas in complex technological contexts, with an emphasis on analyzing the social, legal and environmental impacts of technical decisions.
Develop proposals for professional conduct in line with national and international codes of ethics (OE, IEEE, ITU).

syllabus_topics: Code of Ethics of the Order of Engineers
Ethical frameworks: deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics
Applicability in professional and organizational practice
AI and decision-making algorithms: impartiality, algorithmic justice or non-discrimination
Big Data, surveillance and privacy (briefly includes GDPR and ePrivacy)
Innovating responsibly: legal framework and ethical principles
Technological citizenship, environmental impact, social justice
The engineer as an ethical agent of change
assessment_rules: For assessment throughout the semester, attendance at a minimum of 80% of classes is compulsory. To pass through assessment throughout the semester, students must obtain a final grade of at least 10 out of 20, a minimum grade of 7 out of 20 in the individual written test, and comply with the attendance requirement. Assessment by examination consists of an individual written examination (100%). Students who opted for semester assessment but do not pass may take the examination in the second examination period.
